native_result.query: How did urban land use affect the invasion of different types of introduced plants?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use positively affected the invasion of different types of introduced plants in contrasting ways across the three introduction pathways measured in Catalonia. At the 632-plot level, accumulated urban cover around each plot (urban cover at 1956, 1993, and 2009 within 50 m, 500 m, and 1000 m buffers, plus the change-tier proportions progressive / regressive / no.changes between 1956 and 2009) was positively associated with the per-plot count of introduced species — but the strength and significance of that association differed by pathway: Spearman correlations with urban.2009.500 m were n.unint rho = +0.50, n.gard rho = +0.40, n.agfo rho = +0.11; in the headline 500 m negative-binomial GLM (urban logit + cropland logit + habitat factor + elevation + distance.stream + distance.road + climate) urban slopes were +0.07 (p = 0.26) for Gardening, +0.06 (p = 0.24) for Unintentional, +0.11 (p = 0.46) for AgriForest; and in the stacked long-format pathway-by-urban interaction model (AgriForest reference) the pathway-specific urban slopes were Unintentional +0.193 (p = 0.032) and Gardening +0.146 (p = 0.11), with an interaction Wald chi-square = 4.90, df = 2, p = 0.086. The 1000 m sensitivity check produced near-zero coefficients because that buffer was highly collinear with the habitat-fixed Urban stratum (within-habitat mean urban.2009.1000m = 0.50). The temporal-contingency table (chi-square = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6 x 10^-47) contextualises these pathway effects: Gardening introductions rose from 17 percent to 75 percent of all introductions between Before 1500 and 1985-2019 (18 to 397 introductions), while AgriForest fell from 51 percent to 6 percent (55 to 32). Net: urban land use in Catalonia is associated most strongly with the accumulation of Unintentionally-introduced species and secondarily with Gardening-introduced species, while AgriForest-introduced species show essentially no urban association — a pattern consistent with horticultural and contaminant weed pools colonising expanding urban habitats, and inconsistent with a strong ornamental-specialist effect.
